probes.name: P4a
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Appends the registry to the Stop prompt. Reddens registry-independence FIRST, before the hash assertion can fire, so the two are witnessed separately. This is the drift SLIM5's inline row list exists to avoid.

probes.name: P4b
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: Return ONLY the JSON object the schema requires.
probes.new: Return ONLY the JSON object the schema require.
probes.note: One byte of the shipped prompt. Registry-independence stays GREEN (assertion order puts it first), so this witnesses the hash alone — the check that the shipped bytes are the MEASURED bytes, which is what SD-1 (a) and SD-7 (a) both rest on.

probes.name: P4c
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Drops the strict retry suffix. The first two assertions stay GREEN (they never look at strict), so the retry variant is witnessed on its own.

probes.name: P4d
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: REDEFINED at Step 3. It used to force every event down the Stop branch to witness Step 2's Stop-only scoping. After the held-out validation refuted SLIM5 (28/30 with 2 unsafe against FULL's 29/30 with 0) the routing was reverted, so the claim worth witnessing is the OPPOSITE one: this mutation re-enables the routing, and the guard must redden. It is what stops the revert being quietly undone without AC-7 passing.

probes.name: P5a
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: THESE ARE NOT FORBIDDEN. Do not cite a row against them:
probes.expect_claim: test_slim5_pins_the_not_forbidden_carveouts|"THESE ARE NOT FORBIDDEN. Do not cite a row against them:" in prompt|#0
probes.note: Removes the carve-out header while leaving all three carve-out lines in place, so the sibling assertions stay GREEN and this one reddens alone.

probes.name: P5b
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: except C6, which no go waives
probes.expect_claim: test_slim5_pins_the_c6_waiver_exception|"except C6, which no go waives" in prompt|#0
probes.note: Deletes the single exception to the go-waiver rule. An in-excerpt Cray go would then wave a credential through — the one row SD-7 records as prompt-only precisely because it has no registry home yet.

probes.name: P5c
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.new: Decision and reason should broadly align
probes.expect_claim: test_slim5_pins_the_reason_rules|"Decision and reason MUST agree" in prompt|#0
probes.note: Weakens REASON RULE 1 to a suggestion. Rules 2-4 stay intact so their assertions stay GREEN and this reddens alone.

probes.name: P5d
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: THIS STEP DOES NOT FIRE on an ordinary working turn
probes.new: THIS STEP applies to every turn
probes.expect_claim: test_slim5_pins_the_last_turn_governs_step|"THIS STEP DOES NOT FIRE on an ordinary working turn" in prompt|#0
probes.note: Removes the negative half of STEP 2 while keeping the header, so the first assertion stays GREEN. This is the exact one-sidedness that made SLIM, SLIM3 and SLIM4 pause on ordinary working turns.

probes.name: P5e
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: Default to PAUSE. A spurious pause is cheaper than a spurious proceed. When torn
probes.new: Prefer PAUSE. A spurious pause is cheaper than a spurious proceed. When torn
probes.note: Note the needle length: 'Default to PAUSE' alone occurs TWICE in this file (SLIM5 and the legacy prompt), so a short mutation would hit the wrong prompt and report a meaningless result. The trailing clause survives, keeping the sibling assertion GREEN.

probes.name: P5f
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.note: Renames the one field _validate_dispatch_metadata requires. artifact_kind survives so the sibling assertion stays GREEN. A prompt that stopped naming this field would fail closed to pause and silence the dispatch channel with no error.

probes.name: P6a
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: G3 - reading, opening, quoting or touching anything under docs/strategy/private/
probes.note: Drops a registry row from the PROMPT side. Reddens the drift guard from the direction that actually happens: someone edits the prompt and the registry keeps a row the classifier no longer sees.

probes.name: P6b
probes.subject: .claude/autonomy-triggers.md
probes.new:
| C8 | probe P6b synthetic row | Advisory | Advisory |
| H1 |
probes.note: The SAME claim reddened from the REGISTRY side. Two probes on one assertion is deliberate: it proves the test reads both artifacts. A guard that only ever parsed the prompt would pass this one and fail nothing.

probes.name: P6c
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_sonnet_classifier.py
probes.old: C7 - editing the hooks, gates or classifier under .claude/ that constrain the agent itself
probes.new: C8 - editing the hooks, gates or classifier under .claude/ that constrain the agent itself
probes.note: Renames a prompt-only row. `missing == []` stays GREEN (C8 is still absent from the registry either way), so the prompt-only pin is witnessed alone — that pin is what keeps SD-7's recorded debt visible instead of drifting into permanence.
